item.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones fires back at George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr. injury conspiracy theories
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Cowboys’ Jerry Jones fires back at George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr. injury conspiracy theories appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys are pushing back against speculation surrounding George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. after both players missed Sunday’s victory over the Indianapolis Colts . With the two defenders and offensive playmaker approaching free agency, questions emerged about whether their contract situations influenced their availability. However, team owner Jerry Jones insists their absences had nothing to do with business decisions . During an appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Jones addressed the rumors and dismissed any suggestion of foul play. According to ESPN’s Todd Archer, the Cowboys owner made his position clear: “[It’s] 100 percent injury related. Put it to rest.” His comments came after Dallas secured a 27-23 road win over Indianapolis without two key contributors. Pickens missed the contest while dealing with shoulder and hamstring injuries . He first hurt his shoulder against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 8, while the hamstring problem emerged more recently. Porter, meanwhile, continues to manage an ankle injury that has bothered him for several weeks. He also exited Dallas’ 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on November 1 because of the issue. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Both players could enter the open market after the season. The Cowboys acquired Pickens from the Pittsburgh Steelers before the 2025 campaign. He responded with a career year, posting 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns to earn Pro Bowl honors. This season, he has recorded 39 receptions, 533 yards and two touchdowns in eight games. Dallas acquired Porter from Pittsburgh on September 30. Injuries have limited him to four appearances, with eight tackles and three passes defended. At 4-5, Dallas needs George Pickens ’ explosive playmaking and Joey Porter Jr.’s defensive presence to make a serious playoff push, making their eventual returns crucial to the Cowboys’ postseason hopes. item.title: These North Jersey girls soccer teams will play in sectional finals
item.description: The push for sectional titles continues today across North Jersey, with eight semifinals on the girls soccer schedule. Stay tuned for updates here throughout the day. On Monday, three North Jersey teams advanced in non-public play. Immaculate Heart will face Pingry in the North Non-Public A final, while DePaul and Saddle River Day will square off for the North Non-Public B crown. Ramapo Ramapo saved its best for last. The No. 5 seed Raiders scored three times in the final 10 minutes to pull away for a 4-1 victory over No. 1 Wayne Valley in the North 1, Group 3 semifinals. Senior Bridget Cannon, a Dartmouth track and field commit, ripped in the go-ahead goal before sophomore Lindsay Samala added two insurance tallies. Senior outside back Juniper Chen also scored for the Raiders, which controlled possession with their connected short passing game. The victory was No. 99 for coach Maddie Gibbs, whose team has persevered through an up-and-down season after graduating four Division I players. "We've been struggling with injuries, illness, everything," Gibbs said. "But from early on, we've had a fighting-to-the-last-minute characteristic about this team. And that's definitely one you want on your side come state tournament." Ramapo (11-7-1) has leaned on some young players to fill the gaps, including call-ups from last year's JV county champions. Maybe none have been more important than Samala, who leads the Raiders with 13 goals from the midfield despite missing three weeks with a concussion. "I'm excited because the seniors have really welcomed me, and I just want to keep the season going for them," she said. "I was really upset when I was sitting out because I wanted to be out here, so now I'm just trying to make the most of it." Senior Kaley Potaki has also helped stabilize the midfield since returning from a torn ACL midway through the season. Gibbs estimated that all but three starters have missed time at some point. Now comes a chance to avenge another tournament defeat. Ramapo will face Old Tappan in Friday's sectional final, a rematch of the Bergen County quarterfinals, when the Golden Knights eliminated the Raiders in penalty kicks. Ramapo lost in last year's sectional championship and last captured the North 1, Group 3 title in 2022. “We have a lot of grit and determination,” Cannon said. “We all just want to keep winning and go as far as possible.” Full schedule Madison 5, Lyndhurst 0 Ramapo 4, Wayne Valley 1 Old Tappan 4, Morris Knolls 0 Ridgewood vs. Fair Lawn, 4:15 p.m. Hawthorne vs. Waldwick, 4 p.m. Ramsey vs. Westwood, 6 p.m. Lakeland vs. Montville, 6 p.m. North Arlington vs. Hanover Park, 6 p.m. This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: These North Jersey girls soccer teams will play in sectional finals

item.title: Kirk Cousins Trade Grade: Why Vikings Get A+ and Raiders Settle for C-
item.description: Kirk Cousins Trade Grade: Why Vikings Get A+ and Raiders Settle for C- Monday night’s 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills made the Minnesota Vikings’ quarterback problem impossible to ignore. Less than 24 hours later, they addressed it with a familiar solution. Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick, bringing the 38-year-old quarterback back to the franchise he played for from 2018 through 2023. PFN’s NFL Trade Machine gave Minnesota an A+ for the deal and Las Vegas a C-. Jacob Infante agreed with the result. The Vikings found a clear upgrade at the most important position without giving up premium draft capital, while the Raiders moved a productive starting quarterback at a time when Minnesota had very little leverage to hide its desperation. The Vikings Definitely Won the Kirk Cousins Trade Minnesota is 6-2 despite entering the trade deadline with a quarterback situation that had become increasingly difficult to defend. Kyler Murray had already struggled before suffering a hamstring injury. His 69.9 PFN QB Impact score ranks 27th among qualified quarterbacks this season. That left Carson Wentz to start against Buffalo, and the result was one of the worst quarterback performances of the season. Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions. His 8.9 passer rating was the lowest by a quarterback with at least 25 attempts since Sam Darnold posted a 3.6 against the New England Patriots in 2019. The Vikings don’t need Cousins to suddenly become one of the NFL’s elite quarterbacks. They need competent, consistent play from a position that was threatening to waste everything else the roster has done well. “With Cousins, obviously you’re getting a big upgrade at quarterback,” Infante said. “Not particularly elite, and he certainly has physical limitations at this stage of his career. But in the grand scheme of things, it’s the most important position in football.” That upgrade came at the cost of one third-round pick. Minnesota didn’t have to surrender a first or second-round selection. It didn’t have to bet on a quarterback learning Kevin O’Connell’s offense from scratch in November. The Vikings acquired someone who already knows the head coach, the basic structure of the offense, and its best player. That combination makes the price much easier to justify for a team trying to win now. What Kirk Cousins Gives the Vikings Cousins has been considerably better this season than the quarterback Minnesota is replacing. Through nine starts for Las Vegas, he completed 64.1% of his passes for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. His 80.5 PFN QB Impact score ranks 11th in the league, one spot ahead of Jordan Love and well above Murray. There have been bad games. Cousins threw three interceptions in Sunday’s 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. That performance helped accelerate calls in Las Vegas to turn the offense over to rookie Fernando Mendoza. item.title: Brooklyn Courtnall, daughter of NHL veteran Russ, is back home with San Diego
item.description: Brooklyn Courtnall, daughter of NHL veteran Russ, is back home with San Diego originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Playing professional soccer in Southern California has turned into a homecoming for Brooklyn Courtnall . The defender, 23, is in her second professional season and has returned to familiar ground after Bay FC loaned her to San Diego Wave FC for the rest of the 2026 NWSL season. One part of the move stands out. Courtnall is now training on the same field where she played as a young player growing up. Being back in the region also means her family can come watch her games in person, and that is something she values a great deal. Brooklyn Courtnall Courtnall starred at USC, where she earned All America honors, and she has already played international soccer for Canada. Sports run deep in her family. Her father, Russ Courtnall, played in the NHL and also represented Canada on the international stage. Her own time with the Canadian national team continues a family tradition that started with him. Her career is now growing away from the field as well. Courtnall has become the first female soccer player to partner with Vuori, the California activewear company. The deal connects a Southern California athlete with a brand based in the same state. Courtnall wears Vuori when she is away from training and matches, and she enjoys trying out different items from the company’s collection. She has not made an appearance on behalf of the brand yet. She is looking forward to the opportunities the partnership could bring in the future. The deal shows how business opportunities are expanding for players in women’s soccer. For Courtnall, the main reason she loves her job is simple. She gets to play soccer every day, and she has turned the game she loved as a kid into her profession. item.title: Hornets Snap Skid With Record-Setting Three-Point Night
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets finally stopped the bleeding on Monday night with a massive 124-112 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers. This victory ended a painful six-game losing skid that had the fanbase worried about the season. The team shot a blistering 50 percent from deep, hitting 23 of 46 three-point attempts to bury the Cavs. Veterans Step Up When Stars Sit With Brandon Miller, Dennis Schröder, and other key players out due to injury, the Hornets needed big shots from their veterans. Grayson Allen answered the call with a team-high 27 points while sinking six three-pointers. Naz Reid also dominated inside and out, posting a double-double with 25 points and 13 rebounds, according to NBA.com . According to NBA.com, Reid set the tone early with 15 points in the first quarter alone. These two players combined for 52 points. The offensive explosion was about shooting and flow. The Hornets dished out a season-high 29 assists on their 44 made baskets. This ball movement kept the Cleveland defense off-balance and allowed shooters to find open spots. The team also limited turnovers to just 14, a huge improvement over their league-worst average. The league leader in turnovers per game finally found a way to take care of the ball. Kalkbrenner Controls The Glass By controlling the rebounds, Ryan Kalkbrenner produced the night’s most significant inside effort. He grabbed a game-high 15 rebounds, which included a staggering 10 offensive rebounds. This relentless work on the glass gave Charlotte vital second-chance points that kept the lead growing. Kalkbrenner also recorded three blocked shots and finished with a plus-20 rating. His effort offset the size advantage of the Cavaliers’ frontcourt. Even with a lead of 33 points at one stage, the game got tense in the fourth quarter. The Cavaliers cut the deficit to just eight points before the Hornets pulled away. Five unanswered second-chance points, all set up by Kalkbrenner’s offensive boards, helped seal the win. The Hornets outscored Cleveland 20-7 in second-chance points, a stat that shows their hustle paid off. Kalkbrenner stepped up big time in place of the injured Moussa Diabaté. Young players like Tidjane Salaün also showed promise during the win. Salaün scored a season-high 14 points, all coming in the second quarter to help build the early lead. Christian Anderson Jr. and Sion James added a combined 11 points. The team shot 21 of 41 from deep in the first half, setting a high bar for the rest of the game. Per NBA.com, this win put an end to the hosts’ pesky six-game skid.

item.description: Another eventful NFL trade deadline didn’t disappoint on the final day the league’s teams could swap players ahead of the 4 p.m. ET deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The most impactful move of the final week came down with little more than an hour to spare, the Las Vegas Raiders agreeing to send 38-year-old QB Kirk Cousins back to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft. The deal materialized not 24 hours after the Vikes were embarrassed in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills on “Monday Night Football,” when Minnesota’s offense couldn’t find the end zone and struggled to simply get first downs. But the Vikings weren’t the only team that’s been busy. Here’s a fuller breakdown of this year’s trade deadline winners and losers. WINNERS Kirk Cousins He leaves the rebuilding Raiders, his tutelage of No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza complete, in order to return to Minnesota and pursue the ring that’s eluded him throughout his 15-year career − six of those seasons spent in the Twin Cities. Cousins, who had 20 TD passes in games with the Silver and Black, is playing his best football since 2023, when what had been his presumed final season in Minnesota was cut short by an Achilles injury. Pretty cool that Cousins, who wasn't enthused about leaving for Atlanta in 2024, gets to return and maybe complete some unfinished business. Minnesota Vikings In a stacked division where every other team has bona fide stud at quarterback, the Vikes at least upgrade significantly at the position by bringing Cousins back in light of the failed Kyler Murray experiment . Armed with one of the elite defenses the league has seen in the 21st century, Minnesota at least gives itself a more viable Super Bowl shot than it had 24 hours ago . Former Colts wideouts Both Keenan Allen (San Francisco 49ers) and Josh Downs (Kansas City Chiefs) were rescued from a sinking ship and now both get a shot to pursue a championship and, in Downs' case, maybe a sizable second contract as he plays out the remainder of his rookie deal with Patrick Mahomes throwing to him. item.title: 'It was more of a compliment' - Doc Rivers clarifies Giannis Antetokounmpo insult
item.description: Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Doc Rivers doesn’t want to be blamed for a failed tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks, but he also doesn’t want to be blamed for blaming that failure on Giannis Antetokounmpo. Last week, Rivers went viral for his appearance on The Bill Simmons Podcast, where he claimed Antetokounmpo “ doesn’t have a super-high IQ ,” while also alleging the former NBA MVP was difficult to coach. The hot take about a former league MVP and NBA champion has not been well received, with Rivers accused of failing to hold himself accountable for what was a disappointing head-coaching stop in Milwaukee. Antetokounmpo even admitted the comments rendered him “ speechless. ” Doc Rivers tells Bill Simmons it was so hard for him to coach Giannis Antetokounmpo during his tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks: “He’s not easy. He plays at this crazy downhill pace. He’s really a difficult guy. He has this great passing ability, but he doesn’t have a super-high IQ at the same time. He really has only one way of playing. Every play, he wants to force it. I wish he’d learned how to execute better. “The thing he still needs to learn is the value of execution how important it is, when you’re in practice and at shoot around, to lock in on execution. Now he has a coach who’s as good as there is at execution.” https://t.co/TMdAjkQKDY — Ahmed/The Ears/IG: BigBizTheGod (@big_business_) November 6, 2026 In the wake of causing the controversy, Rivers told ESPN’s Marc J. Spears that he meant to say “feel for the game” instead of “super-high IQ” when talking to Simmons about Antetokounmpo. Rivers also told Spears he has since texted an apology to Antetokounmpo. “I was saying he was one of the most interesting guys,” Rivers explained to Spears. “He makes unbelievable passes, but then at times, because of his force he plays at, it gets in the way of his feel. It was more of a compliment. I hate this and feel bad about it. I apologize for the distraction. I’m not trying to be one.” “The point I was trying to make is whenever you have a great player, you have to fit the team around that great player,” he added . “That is the point I was trying to make. It’s not always easy. It’s a compliment. I’ve been successful and unsuccessful at it. But your job is to create the best team you can possibly create around that great player and his talents.” If all Rivers did was apologize, he would deserve some credit for that. But no one heard Rivers’ comments about Antetokounmpo last week and thought he was trying to compliment the former MVP. Rivers coached Antetokounmpo for parts of three seasons after leaving ESPN for Milwaukee in 2024. Despite joining the Bucks with championship aspirations, Rivers went just 97-103 in Milwaukee before parting ways and retiring from coaching at the end of last season. The Bucks later embraced a full rebuild and sent Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat in the offseason. Rivers is a Hall of Fame NBA head coach, winning a championship with the Boston Celtics

item.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
item.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. I ’ve been playing alongside him at Bayern for years, in the holding midfield role, and it’s incredibly enjoyable. We complement each other ex tremely well. That’s why I think this debate is unnecessary,” Pavlović said (as captured by @i MiaSanMia ). It is a straightforward endorsement from Pavlović, who has developed into an important midfield option himself. There is room for different partners hips and competition for places, but he is not suggesting that Kimmich’s leadership or importance should be questioned.
